conversationalSummary.text: It’s probably not worth chasing a session today, even though Rey Cortiço at lunch is the best of what’s available. Wind looks like the main problem and Surfline consistency is poor, so you’re likely to get messy conditions. Before you bother leaving, do a quick check on the Surfline cams and MEO Beachcam—unless they look surprisingly much better, I’d save the drive.

best.explanation: Rey Cortiço looks like a small north coast window for Rare window, Low confidence: 0.3-0.6 m, 18 kJ, 10 s period, lully 1/100, and wind is the main risk.  An open beach break where the sandbanks decide everything; this is best for quiet, punchy peaks when Lagide is too small; 10-13s at mid tide also works on Belgas, but low tide is not a deal-breaker, so checking exposed beaches makes sense.  Watch: Surfline consistency is lully; wind angle is poor for this spot.
best.shortExplanation: Rey Cortiço is worth a quick check for lunch, but it is not a guaranteed session.  Treat it as a check-first call rather than a sure thing.  Wind is the main thing to watch.  The tide should let the sandbars work without overdoing it.
warnings: wind angle is poor for this spot
